How long do implants last?

A crown covers a single damaged tooth. A bridge replaces one or more missing teeth by attaching to the teeth or implants on either side of the gap.

faq: What are signs of sleep apnea?
Loud, chronic snoring and trouble breathing through the night are common signs. If you or your partner notice them, it’s worth getting checked.
How does an oral appliance help?
A custom oral appliance gently holds the lower jaw forward to help keep the airway open during sleep.
Is it an alternative to a CPAP?

An oral appliance may be an option for adults with obstructive sleep apnea who cannot tolerate CPAP or prefer an alternative. A sleep physician and dentist can help decide whether it is suitable for you.
Is sleep apnea dangerous?
It can be. That’s why we encourage anyone with chronic snoring to get examined and treated.
Do I need to see another doctor?
Sleep apnea is diagnosed by a physician. We can examine you and, if needed, refer you to a specialist such as an ENT.

faq: What is TMJ disorder?
TMJ disorder, or TMD, is a problem with the joint that connects your jaw to your skull. It often causes pain, clicking and headaches.
How does a night guard help?
It realigns the jaw joint and takes pressure off your back teeth, so your jaw can relax and stop clenching while you sleep.
Why do I clench my jaw at night?
You have little control over your movements while you sleep, which is why nighttime clenching is one of the biggest reasons TMD continues and gets worse.
How soon will I feel better?
Many patients notice relief soon after they start wearing their guard. We’ll check in and adjust it if needed.
Can TMJ affect eating or speaking?
Yes. TMD can make chewing, swallowing and speaking harder, which is another reason to get it treated.

faq: What is TMJ disorder?
TMJ disorder, or TMD, is a problem with the joint that connects your jaw to your skull. It often causes pain, clicking and headaches.
How does a night guard help?
It realigns the jaw joint and takes pressure off your back teeth, so your jaw can relax and stop clenching while you sleep.
Why does my jaw hurt more in the morning?
You have little control over your movements while you sleep, so nighttime clenching is a common cause of morning jaw pain.
How soon will I feel better?
Many patients notice relief soon after they start wearing their guard. We’ll check in and adjust it if needed.

She’s from a small town in Missouri and moved back from Colorado after seven years there.
creds: Bachelor of Science, University of Missouri. Doctor of Dental Surgery, UMKC School of Dentistry
General dentistry and patients who feel nervous about the dentist
Hiking with her Bernese Mountain Dog, Moose, skiing and the outdoors

doctors.full: Dr. Owen Lonergan, MPH, DMD, MD
doctors.short: Board-certified oral surgeon and former UMKC clinical faculty.
doctors.bio: Dr. Lonergan is a board-certified oral and maxillofacial surgeon who treats implant and oral surgery patients at our Westport office. After residency he joined the UMKC School of Dentistry as clinical faculty, teaching oral surgery to dental students. He grew up in Texas and lives in Kansas City with his wife and daughter.
creds: B.S. in Biology, UC San Diego. DMD and Master of Public Health, Arizona School of Dentistry & Oral Health. MD, UMKC School of Medicine
Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery residency, UMKC
Diplomate, American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons, Greater Kansas City Society of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons

doctors.short: Board-certified oral surgeon for implants, grafting and jaw surgery.
doctors.bio: Dr. Lucaci is a board-certified oral and maxillofacial surgeon. He performs implant surgery, bone grafting, wisdom teeth extractions and jaw surgery, and offers IV sedation for a more relaxed procedure. He became an oral surgeon because it’s a cross between medicine and dentistry. Born and raised in Kampala, Uganda, he enjoys golf and travel.
creds: Bachelor of Dental Surgery, Makerere University. DDS with honors, UMKC School of Dentistry. MD, University of Missouri
Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery residency, UMKC
American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery
American Dental Association, American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons, American College of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons, Missouri and Kansas Dental Associations

doctors.short: Sedation certified, at our Westport office 1 to 2 days a month.
doctors.bio: Dr. Baker is the primary dentist at ECare and holds her sedation certification for Missouri. She brings her sedation expertise to our Westport office about 1 to 2 days a month, with a gentle approach that helps even the most anxious patients get the care they need.
creds: A calm, supportive visit for patients who feel anxious

general.p: Dr. Hunter McAreavy leads general dentistry at our Westport office and has a passion for helping patients who feel nervous about the dentist. Whoever you see that day, our hygienists, assistants and care coordinators take the time to explain each step.

surgical.p: Dr. Owen Lonergan and Dr. Patrick Lucaci are the oral surgeons at our Westport location, so your surgery happens in the same place as the rest of your care. Our surgical assistant and care coordinators guide you from your consultation to your follow-up visits.

sedation.h2: Calm care from a team that gets it.
sedation.p: Dr. Shaley Baker holds a Missouri Sedation Certification and provides sedation at our Westport location about one to two days a month. Dr. Hunter McAreavy and our team know many patients feel nervous, so we explain every step and never rush you.
